recreation_brief:
1. Set the slide background to light grey (#F2F2F2).
2. Place the title "Accuracy" at the top center-left (approx. 5–15% slide height) in large, bold, red (#C00000) sans-serif type.
3. Add a grey rectangular definition strip directly below the title spanning the full width (approx. 15–28% slide height). Inside it, place the text "Correctly Classified (Positive & Negative)" with a red (#C00000) underline beneath it, then place "Total Number of Samples" below that line.
4. In the left column (approx. 30–95% slide height, left 45% width), place the red bold header "Meaning" at the top of the column.
5. Below "Meaning", place the line "How Accurate is the Classification (for Both Positive and Negative Classes)" in black, with the words "Positive" and "Negative" colored blue (#0070C0).
6. Place the text "Correctly Classified" in red italic directly above the formula box.
7. Add a white box with a red (#C00000) border in the middle-left. Inside, place the equation "Accuracy = (TP + TN) / (TP + FP + TN + FN)" in black, and place "All Samples" in red italic below the equation.
8. Add a light blue (#DEEBF7) box in the lower-left, below the formula box. Inside, place the calculation "Accuracy= (18+60)/(18+12+60+10) = 78/100 = 78%" in black.
9. To the right of the light blue box, place "Accuracy of ALL Classes" in red italic.
10. Add a yellow (#FFF2CC) box at the bottom-left. Inside, place three lines of black text: "What About Precision of Positive Class ONLY Results?", "What About Recall % of Positive Samples ?", and "Conclusion: Accuracy is Good but Not Sufficient" with the final line in red (#C00000).
11. In the extreme top-right corner (approx. 5–10% slide height), place a yellow (#FFF2CC) circle containing the number "6" in black.
12. Below the slide number, in the top-right region (approx. 10–50% slide height, right 30% width), place the first confusion matrix (symbolic). Use a table with black borders and white cell fills. Header row: "Predicted as" spanning two columns labeled "P" and "N". Row headers: "Actual" with sub-rows "P" and "N". Cells: top-left "TP" with green fill (#00B050), top-right "FN", bottom-left "FP", bottom-right "TN" with green fill (#00B050). All text black.
13. Directly below the first matrix, place the second confusion matrix (numeric) with identical headers and structure. Cells: top-left "18" with green fill (#00B050), top-right "12", bottom-left "10", bottom-right "60" with green fill (#00B050). All text black.
14. In the bottom-right region (approx. 55–95% slide height, right 45% width), place two decision-tree diagrams side by side.
15. Left tree: place the label "Positive" in red (#C00000) above the root. Draw a root node as a red (#C00000) circle containing "30". Draw a left branch to a red (#C00000) circle containing "18" with the label "TP" beside it. Draw a right branch to a green (#00B050) circle containing "12" with the label "FN" beside it.
16. Right tree: place the label "Negative" in green (#00B050) above the root. Draw a root node as a green (#00B050) circle containing "70". Draw a left branch to a green (#00B050) circle containing "60" with the label "TN" beside it. Draw a right branch to a red (#C00000) circle containing "10" with the label "FP" beside it.
17. Above each tree diagram, place one small grey-outline airplane icon: above the "Positive" tree place an icon with a star, and above the "Negative" tree place an icon with windows.
